description:
FILED s477 (Fable, 2026-09-08) from the s473b review probes.  PRE-EXISTING: identical on main c8d11c31 and on the s473b tree 3b153d7f (which fixed the INTERMEDIATE vivification of `$h{a}{b} &&= 1`, #1241 -- $h{a} is now created as perl does; the LAST level's key is this residue).

Reproducer (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL, default AND PCL_OPT=none):
  my %f1; $f1{x} &&= 1;    print exists $f1{x} ? "key" : "nokey";   # perl: key     PCL: nokey
  my %f4; $f4{c}{d} &&= 1; print join(",", keys %f4), " ", (exists $f4{c}{d} ? "inner" : "no-inner");
                                                                   # perl: c inner   PCL: c no-inner
Only `&&=` exposes it: `||=` and `//=` store exactly when the element is false/undef, so their key always exists afterwards.

Why: perl compiles the left operand of andassign with OPf_MOD (lvalue), so pp_helem fetches with lval=1 and CREATES the entry before the value is tested; PCL's p-and-assign reads the place with the plain rvalue accessor (%p-elem-place-form binds container+key once, #1152, but the read is `(p-gethash C K)`, which does not create) and stores only on the true branch.

Fix shape: in p-and-assign (and, for symmetry, p-or-assign / p-//=) read the element through its EAGER `-box` accessor (`p-gethash-box` / `p-aref-box`, the same pair `for ($h{zz})` and `\$h{zz}` use) so the key exists after the read -- the store-back then writes through the same box.  Probe the array twin (`$a[5] &&= 1` grows @a to 6 in perl), the deref spellings, and that a DEFINED false value is untouched.  Guard rows in Pl/t/autoviv-02.t, inverse-verified.  Bars: runtime-only -> gate + sweep + companion op/hashassign.t op/aassign.t; ir-conform.  Low priority: `exists` after a non-storing `&&=` is rare in real code.
subject: `$h{x} &&= 1` on an absent/false element does not CREATE the key; perl evaluates a compound assignment's element in LVALUE context and creates it even when nothing is stored (exists $h{x} is true after; nested `$h{c}{d} &&= 1` creates $h{c}{d} too)
